title: Colorado PUC Decision R26-0039: Recommended Decision Adopting Rules and Closing Proceeding
summary: Recommended Decision Adopting Rules and Closing Proceeding
text:
Decision No. R26-0039 
BEFORE THE PUBLIC UTILITIES COMMISSION OF THE STATE OF COLORADO 
PROCEEDING NO. 25R-0325R 
IN THE MATTER OF THE PROPOSED AMENDMENTS TO THE RULES REGULATING 
RAILROADS, RAIL FIXED GUIDEWAYS, TRANSPORTATION BY RAIL, AND 
RAIL CROSSINGS, 4 CODE OF COLORADO REGULATIONS 723-7, TO IMPLEMENT 
HOUSE BILL 25-1110. 
RECOMMENDED DECISION 
ADOPTING RULES AND CLOSING PROCEEDING 
Issued Date: January 26, 2026 

I. 
STATEMENT 
A. 
Background 
1. 
On August 6, 2025, the Public Utilities Commission (“Commission”) issued the 
Notice of Proposed Rulemaking (“NOPR”) that commenced this proceeding.1 In the NOPR, the 
Commission proposed to amend the rules applicable to Rules Regulating Railroads, Rail Fixed 
Guideways, Transportation by Rail, and Rail Crossings, 4 Code of Colorado Regulations 723-7 
(“Rail Rules”). The purpose of the amendments is to implement the allocation of costs to 
maintain railroad crossings in the state enacted in House Bill (“HB”) 25-1110, and codified at 
§ 40-4-106(5) and (6), C.R.S. Specifically, the Commission proposed to add a new definition of 
“maintain” to Rule 7201, modified paragraph 7211(j), added new paragraph 7211(k), and 
renumbered the remaining paragraphs in Rule 7211. The NOPR scheduled a public comment 
hearing for September 22, 2025, at 11:30 a.m. 

1 See Decision No. C25-0570.

2. 
On same day that the NOPR issued in this proceeding, the Commission issued 
temporary rules that are exactly the same as the rules proposed in the NOPR. The temporary 
rules were issued with Decision No. C25-0572 issued in Proceeding No. 25R-0326R on 
August 6, 2025. 
3. 
Subsequently, the Office of the Attorney General issued an opinion that the 
proposed rules and the temporary rules were not consistent with HB 25-1110. 
4. 
The Commission then issued amended temporary rules in Decision No. C25-0617 
issued in Proceeding No. 25R-0352R on August 27, 2025. The new temporary rules fixed the 
issue identified by the Attorney General’s opinion. 
5. 
The undersigned Administrative Law Judge (“ALJ”) held the hearing on 
September 22, 2025, starting at 11:30 a.m. At the hearing, Commission Staff requested that the 
Commission adopt the changes to the proposed rules contained in the amended rules issued in 
Proceeding No. 25R-0352R. The ALJ agreed. The ALJ then proposed changes to temporary 
rules 7211(j) & (k) from Proceeding No. 25R-0352R as follows (redlining showing changes 
proposed in NOPR and bluelining showing changes proposed by the ALJ): 
(j) 
For all road authorities that are not local governmentsIf the road 
authority is other than a local government, tThe total costs to 
maintain an existing crossing surface, including, but not limited to, 
materials, labor, traffic control, railroad flagging, and any 
necessary permits, shall be shared equally between the railroad, 
railroad corporation, rail fixed guideway, transit agency, or owner 
of the track, on the one hand, and the road authority, on the other 
hand. 
(k) 
For all local government road authoritiesIf the road authority is a 
local government, the railroad, railroad corporation, rail fixed 
guideway, transit agency, or owner of the track is responsible for 
all costs to maintain the portion of the existing crossing that is 
between the ends of the railroad ties. The local government road

authority is responsible for the costs to maintain the portion of the 
existing crossing that is outside of the ends of the railroad ties. 
The ALJ requested written comments regarding the proposed changes above and established 
deadlines for initial and response written comments of October 31, 2025 and November 7, 2025, 
respectively. Finally, the ALJ continued the hearing until November 19, 2025, at 11:30 a.m. 
6. 
On October 3, 2025, the ALJ issued Decision No. R25-0709-I that memorialized 
the decisions made at the September 22, 2025 remote public comment hearing. 
7. 
On November 18, 2025, Union Pacific Railroad Company (“Union Pacific”) filed 
a Motion to Continue the first continued November 19, 2025 public comment hearing (“Motion 
to Continue”). 
8. 
On November 19, 2025, Union Pacific filed a Reservation of Rights. 
9. 
On November 19, 2025, the ALJ held the first continued remote public comment 
hearing, granted Union Pacific’s Motion to Continue, and continued the hearing until 
December 9, 2025 at 11:30 a.m. Nobody provided oral comments regarding the proposed rule 
changes at the first continued public comment hearing. 
10. 
On December 2, 2025, the ALJ issued Decision No. R25-0856-I that 
memorialized the decisions made at the November 19, 2025 first continued remote public 
comment hearing. 
11. 
On December 9, 2025, the ALJ held the second continued remote public comment 
hearing. Again, nobody provided oral comments regarding the proposed rule changes. At the 
conclusion of the December 9, 2025 second continued remote public comment hearing, the ALJ 
adjourned the hearing. 
12. 
Nobody has filed written comments in this proceeding.

B. 
Analysis 
13. 
The ALJ has carefully reviewed the proposed rule changes. Based on that review, 
and the absence of any comments requesting changes to the proposed rules or the changes to 
those rules proposed by the ALJ, the ALJ will adopt the changes proposed in Decision No. 
C25-0617 and amended in Decision No. R25-0709-I. 
14. 
Pursuant to the provisions of § 40-6-109, C.R.S., it is recommended that the 
Commission enter the following order and adopt the attached rules. 
II. 
ORDER 
A. 
The Commission Orders That: 
1. 
The Rules Regulating Railroads, Rail Fixed Guideways, Transportation by Rail, 
and Rail Crossings attached to this Recommended Decision are adopted. 
2. 
The rules in legislative (strikethrough/redline) format are attached to this 
Recommended Decision as Attachment A. The rules in final format are attached to this 
Recommended Decision as Attachment B. They are also available in the Commission’s E-Filings 
system at: 
https://www.dora.state.co.us/pls/efi/EFI.Show_Docket?p_session_id=&p_docket_id=25R-0325R 
3. 
Proceeding No. 25R-0325R is closed. 
4. 
This Recommended Decision shall be effective on the day it becomes the 
Decision of the Commission, if that is the case, and is entered as of the date above.

5. 
As provided by § 40-6-109, C.R.S., copies of this Recommended Decision shall 
be made available to all parties in the proceeding, who may file exceptions to it. 
a. If no exceptions are filed within 20 days after service or within any extended 
period of time authorized, or unless the decision is stayed by the Commission 
upon its own motion, the recommended decision shall become the decision of 
the Commission and subject to the provisions of § 40-6-114, C.R.S. 
b. If a party seeks to amend, modify, annul, or reverse basic findings of fact in its 
exceptions, that party must request and pay for a transcript to be filed, or the 
parties may stipulate to portions of the transcript according to the procedure 
stated in § 40-6-113, C.R.S. If no transcript or stipulation is filed, the 
Commission is bound by the facts set out by the administrative law judge and 
the parties cannot challenge these facts. This will limit what the Commission 
can review if exceptions are filed. 
6. 
If exceptions to this Decision are filed, they shall not exceed 30 pages in length, 
unless the Commission for good cause shown permits this limit to be exceeded.
